note: What a server streaming a match sends to carry one fragment of a chunk or key frame of recorded messages (see spec/spectating.md). A chunk's facts come from its fragment 0. The fragments of a chunk come in order from 0, and the chunk is complete at index fragments − 1. A new fragment 0 drops an unfinished chunk, and a fragment with no chunk begun has no effect. The header carries zero.

fields.name: chunk
fields.note: The chunk's id, or the key frame's. Chunk 0 is dropped; chunks play in order from the one a client starts at, and a missing one after it stalls the stream. Key frames count separately, from 1.

fields.name: fragments
fields.note: How many fragments the chunk is cut into.

fields.name: index
fields.note: This fragment's place, from 0.

fields.name: kind
fields.note: What the chunk is.

3.name: endOfStartup
3.note: The last chunk of the match's setting up.

4.name: gameStart
4.note: The chunk the match proper begins with.

5.name: startup
5.note: A chunk of the match's setting up.

fields.name: size
fields.note: The whole chunk's size in bytes.

fields.name: duration
fields.note: Seconds the chunk covers. A client reads it only from fragment 0, and uses it only for the match's last chunk: the match ends that many seconds after that chunk starts. A value too large holds a client that joins near the end on its loading screen.

fields.name: nextChunk
fields.note: For a key frame, the ordinary chunk to go on from. Where zero or less, a client takes key frame interval over chunk interval, times the key frame's id less one, plus the start-game chunk: the one StreamChunkRange names, or the last chunk of kind 4 to arrive.

fields.name: data
fields.note: This fragment's bytes of the chunk, to the end of the message.
